text: Right now, you're spinning around with the Earth at up to sixteen hundred and seventy kilometers an hour. So what if it just stopped?
Stop it suddenly, and everything not bolted to the bedrock keeps going east. You, your house, and the ocean.
Luckily, nothing can stop a planet that fast. Unluckily, let's slow it down gently instead.
Spinning is why Earth bulges in the middle. It's about twenty-one kilometers fatter at the equator.
Stop the spin, and that bulge sinks. The oceans slide downhill, toward the poles.
Two giant polar oceans. Most of Europe and Russia, underwater.
And around the middle, one brand new supercontinent, wrapped around the whole planet.
Then there's the Sun. With no spin, one day lasts a whole year. Six months of daylight, then six months of night.
